title: A Reflective Personal Statement

opts: В течение двух лет до этого

writingModel: Who I Was and Who I Am Becoming — Amir Bekzhanov

When I first arrived at WKU two years ago, I had a clear image of who I was and what I wanted: a computer science student from Aktobe who was going to graduate, find a good job, and return home. I had been building towards this plan for years. I had studied hard, had chosen my subjects carefully, and had arrived with my future, as I imagined it, largely planned.

The plan was not wrong. But it was incomplete. What I had not anticipated was how much the experience of being here — the conversations, the difficulties, the unexpected things I have found myself caring about — would reshape not the plan, but the person who was following it.

Over the past two years, I have been changing in ways that are difficult to describe precisely. I arrived speaking English as a learned system. I have been using it as a working tool. The shift happened without my noticing. One afternoon I realised I had been writing documentation for three hours without once stopping to translate. That moment told me something about fluency that no test result has.

I have also been discovering things about myself that I did not know before I left home. I had assumed I was someone who worked best alone. But since I began collaborating on projects with classmates — people who had been studying the same problems from completely different angles — I have found that I think better in dialogue than in isolation. The friction of other perspectives has been producing better work than I had ever produced alone.

What I have learned most clearly is this: the person I was when I arrived had been formed by everything I had experienced before — my family, my school, my city. The person I am becoming is being formed by everything that has been happening since. Both of these people are me. But the second one is more interesting.

Going forward, I intend to continue this process deliberately. I have been developing skills in machine learning that I plan to apply in contexts I have not yet imagined. I have been building relationships with people whose work I admire and whose questions challenge me. I have been reading — more widely than any course has demanded — because I have realised that the most important parts of my education have been the ones that nobody assigned.
I do not know exactly who I will be in four years. But I know that I have been learning how to not be afraid of that uncertainty. That, more than any technical skill, feels like progress.

"I have realised..." = Present Perfect Simple. A completed discovery with present relevance.
"I had assumed I was someone who..." — what you used to think, now proved incomplete or wrong.
"Since I began X, I have found..." / "Since arriving, I have been discovering..." ✅
"I intend to..." / "I plan to..." / "I am going to..." — clear intention for the future.
